body:
OWNER CORRECTION WITH BEHAVIORAL EVIDENCE: the statement that dynamic surface detail is only an unexposed app parameter is too optimistic. On current storymodel4s main 61e967c, SurfaceDetail is a receipted but semantically inert axis.

Static trace: AtlasCompiler reads spec.zoom.narrative to build marks at atlas.scala:366. The only production uses of spec.zoom.surface are the configuration checksum at :770 and the textual twin via scene.zoom at :793. A repository-wide Scala search finds no branch on Hidden, Sentences, or Tokens in mark compilation. NarrativeScene carries the enum, but no sentence/token surface packet.

Behavioral probe in fixturesJVM console at grakern 0329c43: compile the WOG Scene view three times with Hidden, Sentences, Tokens. Result:
- mark counts Vector(83, 83, 83)
- hidden.marks == sentences.marks: true
- hidden.marks == tokens.marks: true
- navigation equal across all three: true
- selectionPlacements equal across all three: true
- configuration checksums distinct: 3

So simply adding a StoryAtlas selector would create three different receipts and titles for the same representation. That is a ghost axis and fails the accepted product requirement.

Revised routing for local bd-01M16KD7WBWKTQC6CENE9V67Q0: do not begin with the control. First dispose where the exact surface packet lives. A consumer-owned implementation is possible only if ADR 0002 explicitly defines SurfaceDetail as a renderer-layer projection of canonical SurfaceAtlas units with stable ids and no inference; otherwise storymodel4s.view must compile surface primitives or an evidence-backed surface layer into NarrativeScene. Then StoryAtlas exposes the axis and proves representation change plus Address conservation.

This remains separate from recall, but it is not nearly free. I will not ship receipt-only zoom.
